purpose: B01/#1046: permitted module edges, exported port, external-crate port and Cargo feature configuration of the native desktop crate (src-tauri), enforced through the normal local boundaries lane by the Rust-aware analyzer (scripts/nemo/lib/boundaries-rust.cjs). Module identity and layers come from rust.profile.json; this policy also pins the application_mcp.rs <-> nemo-mcp crate boundary (the application MCP adapter port) that P12's intra-crate-only analyzer did not previously cover.
profileModulesNote: The five profile modules under sourceDir. rust.desktop.build (src-tauri/build.rs) is outside sourceDir (dir 'src-tauri', not 'src-tauri/src') and is not part of this crate's own module graph; it is named in unanalyzedModules below as a census entry only.

desktop-shell.meaning: lib.rs/main.rs (shell), media_probe.rs/vectorize.rs/video_decode.rs (media) and task_runtime.rs (tasks) may depend on each other and on the adapters layer (lib.rs declares `mod application_mcp;`), never directly on tests

adapters.meaning: application_mcp.rs has no intra-crate `crate::`/`super::`/`self::` references at all; its only crate-level dependency is the external nemo-mcp port, governed separately by externalCratePorts below, not by this layer graph

permittedEdges.note: Observed at adoption from `mod …;` declarations in lib.rs (the crate root) and `use super::*;` in task_runtime/tests.rs (analyzer output). Layer rules are the enforced contract; this list documents which edges exist so a new one is a visible diff. Plain function-call references such as `video_decode::VideoSessions::default()` in lib.rs are unqualified sibling-module paths, not `crate::`/`super::`/`self::` paths, so they are outside what this analyzer resolves and add no edges beyond the `mod …;` declarations already listed.
edges: rust.desktop.shell -> rust.desktop.media (lib.rs: mod video_decode; mod media_probe; mod vectorize;)

exportedPort.source: src-tauri/src/lib.rs has no `pub use` re-exports; the Tauri command functions registered via `tauri::generate_handler![...]` are Tauri's own invoke registration, not a Rust module export

features.declaredNote: src-tauri/Cargo.toml has no [features] table; any cfg(feature = "…") in the crate would therefore reference an undeclared feature and fail. The crate uses no feature cfgs today, only the four plain predicates below.

nemo_mcp.note: The nemo-mcp crate's transport port (rust.mcp.transport, nemo-mcp/src/lib.rs publicApi) as consumed today by application_mcp.rs: the `use nemo_mcp::{contract::{ApplicationRequest, ApplicationResponse}, registry::{self, Endpoint, Registration}, wire};` block and the inline `nemo_mcp::BUILD_SOURCE_ID` reference. A declared item covers itself and any deeper path under it (e.g. `registry` covers `registry::Endpoint`). Only rust.desktop.mcp.adapter may reference nemo_mcp at all; any other module doing so is an external-crate-violation, and rust.desktop.mcp.adapter reaching an undeclared nemo_mcp path is a private-port-access violation.

unanalyzedModulesNote: Census entries only, never graphed by this analyzer: rust.desktop.build is the Cargo build script (outside sourceDir, no crate module graph); rust.mcp.transport is the whole nemo-mcp crate, referenced here only as the target of externalCratePorts.nemo_mcp and not itself given an intra-crate policy by this file.
